Hello

Why not structure the dataset differently, i.e. have separate strata for=20
every forest-season combination? Then you could output separate estimates=
=20
for every forest-season-species combination.

There is another trick you can use to "fool" DISTANCE. Let us say you wan=
t=20
only the for forest 1 for all seasons, and need bootstrap totals for tha=
t=20
combination using a pooled detection function. You can temporarily set th=
e=20
surface areas of the other strata to near 0, like 0.0001 unit or somethin=
g.=20
That way it will use the data in the other strata in the detection functi=
on=20
but the abundance in these strata will be 0. This is a useful trick if yo=
u=20
need a subtotal of your strata as it saves you the trouble of calculating=
=20
the subtotals outside of DISTANCE in a spreadsheet.

Or perhaps I have misunderstood what you are trying to do here.
